VBO:0201179.summary: Territorial and watchful, the Sardinian Shepherd Dog is known locally as the Cane Fonnese. Its guarding instinct and wariness of strangers reflect work protecting flocks and property. Sardinian keepers long selected these dogs for working ability and behavior, so the population retained considerable variation in appearance before a provisional standard was drawn up.
VBO:0201179.shortDescription: A territorial Sardinian flock and property guardian, the Cane Fonnese was long selected for work and remains wary of strangers.

sources.evidence: Entire eight-page actual normative PDF and whole renders personally read. Pages3–5 work/guarding/intelligence; natural triangular pendant ears, developed mildly rectangular medium body/strong functional legs/compact oval feet/coarse goatlike double coat and black/ash/honey choices. Page5 full natural tail just beyond hock, lower set tapering pump-handle at rest, never erect/amputated; natural anure/brachyure explicitly acknowledged. Pages1/7/8 drawings, not adult photos. Historical ancestry/training legends/clinical absolutes/individual-safety claims excluded.

sources.title: Dreger et al.2016 — Genomic history of the Sardinian Fonni dog

Figure1B smooth coat developed standing coarsebody;1C rough coat developed head/neck only. Subsequent genomic results not claimed fully read or adopted.
